source: A mixture is two or more things mixed together that keep their own properties. In a solution, one thing dissolves evenly into another, like salt in water. The total mass stays the same.
Thinking dissolved salt is gone. It is still there, spread out in pieces too small to see: the water tastes salty and the mass has not changed.
Stir raisins into cereal and you have a mixture: each part keeps its own look and taste, and you can pick the raisins back out.
A mixture is two or more things mixed together that keep their own properties. A solution is a mixture in which one thing dissolves evenly into another, like sugar in tea.
Mixtures you can pick apart, and solutions you cannot see the parts of.
You can separate mixtures: pick out pieces by hand, pour through a sieve or filter, pull iron filings out with a magnet, or let the water evaporate to get dissolved salt back.
The salt in salt water is not gone. It broke into pieces too small to see, spread through the water. Taste it, or let the water dry up, and the salt is there.
You stir 20 g of salt into 200 g of water. What is the mass of the salt water?
Dissolving does not destroy any matter.
Thinking dissolved salt has disappeared, so the salt water weighs the same as the water alone.
